questions.text: What does Aizat Sarsenova study at WKU?
questions.hint: "I study Ecology at WKU in Uralsk." — Aizat introduces herself in the first paragraph.

questions.text: In Astana, winter temperatures can drop to minus thirty degrees or lower.
questions.hint: "In winter, the temperature drops to MINUS THIRTY DEGREES or even lower." — Aizat describes her home city's climate.

questions.text: What was the weather like when Aizat first arrived in Uralsk in September?
opts: Cold and rainy with grey skies
Mild and warm — about eighteen degrees
questions.correct: Mild and warm — about eighteen degrees
questions.hint: "When I arrived in September, the weather was mild and surprisingly warm... the temperature was around eighteen degrees."

questions.text: The first snow of the season in Uralsk fell on a ___ morning in November.
questions.hint: "The first snow fell on a TUESDAY morning — light, dry flakes that covered the ground in just a few hours."

questions.text: What is Timur Bekzhanov's favourite season for fashion?
questions.hint: "AUTUMN is my favourite season for fashion. The weather is cool and crisp — usually between five and fifteen degrees."

questions.text: Timur's waterproof jacket is dark green with a hood.
questions.hint: "A long WATERPROOF JACKET — dark NAVY BLUE, with a hood." — NOT dark green. Dark navy blue is the correct colour.

questions.text: Timur's cream-coloured woollen scarf was knitted by his ___ in Kostanay.
questions.hint: "It's woollen and very warm. My GRANDMOTHER knitted it for me in Kostanay." — Timur tells Aizat about his scarf.

questions.text: What is Timur's main advice for dressing well as a student on a budget?
opts: Buy one very expensive coat and nothing else
Choose fashionable items in bright colours
Buy practical, well-made items in neutral colours
Only wear clothes from sports brands
questions.correct: Buy practical, well-made items in neutral colours
questions.hint: "I buy practical, well-made clothes in neutral colours — dark blue, grey, white, brown, black — that work in all weather."

questions.text: What is the temperature outside when Gulnara and Arsen meet?
questions.hint: "A thick orange sweater, dark jeans, and my brown leather boots. It's MINUS SIX outside — very cold!" — Arsen tells Gulnara.

questions.text: Arsen's wool scarf was bought at a market in Astana.
questions.hint: "It's pure wool — my mum bought it at the market in ALMATY." — NOT Astana. The scarf comes from the Almaty market.

questions.text: Arsen checks his weather forecast ___ every morning before he gets out of bed.
questions.hint: "I check my forecast APP before I even get out of bed." — Arsen describes his morning routine to Gulnara.

questions.text: What is the weather forecast for Saturday?
opts: Sunny and calm with plus four degrees
Heavy snow all day with minus ten degrees
Partly cloudy, minus two degrees, and quite windy
Foggy and freezing with minus fifteen degrees
questions.correct: Partly cloudy, minus two degrees, and quite windy
questions.hint: "Saturday is going to be PARTLY CLOUDY with a temperature of MINUS TWO DEGREES. And QUITE WINDY." — Zulfiya reads the forecast.

questions.text: Sunday's forecast is colder and windier than Saturday.
questions.hint: "Sunday is MUCH BETTER! SUNNY and CALM — almost no wind. The temperature RISES to PLUS FOUR." — Sunday is warmer and calmer, not colder and windier.

questions.text: What is the temperature on Saturday morning before noon?
questions.hint: "Saturday morning is the coldest part — MINUS FIVE before noon. But it gets warmer through the afternoon." — Zulfiya explains.

questions.text: Which sentence uses the adjective correctly?
opts: The weather cold is very today.
The very cold is weather today.
The weather is very cold today.
Today very is the weather cold.
questions.correct: The weather is very cold today.
questions.hint: Adjective AFTER "be": Subject + be + adjective. "The weather IS very cold." ✅ Adjectives in English always come before the noun OR after "be" — never at the end alone.

questions.text: "Three warm coats" is correct English — adjectives do NOT change for plural nouns.
questions.hint: TRUE! English adjectives NEVER change for plural. "three WARM coats" ✅ — NOT "three warms coats." Only the noun gets -s. This is a key difference from Russian and Kazakh!

questions.text: Saturday is ___ than today — the forecast shows minus two versus zero degrees.
questions.hint: cold = 1 syllable → comparative: cold + ER = COLDER. "Saturday is COLDER THAN today." ✅ Short adjectives use -er, NOT "more cold" — that's a common mistake!

questions.text: Write the comparative form of "hot": "July in Uralsk is ___ than October."
questions.hint: hot = CVC (h-o-t): 1 syllable, consonant-vowel-consonant → DOUBLE the final consonant + er: hot → HOTT-ER. ✅ "hoter" is wrong — the t must be doubled!

questions.text: "Uralsk is ___ cold ___ Astana in winter" — Uralsk has milder winters.
questions.hint: "Uralsk is NOT AS cold AS Astana." ✅ Both AS are required. This structure means Uralsk is less cold — Astana is colder. NOT AS + adjective + AS.

questions.text: "The most comfortable coat" is the correct superlative form of the adjective "comfortable".
questions.hint: TRUE! comfortable = long adjective (4 syllables) → superlative: THE MOST comfortable ✅ NOT "the comfortablest." Long adjectives always use THE MOST, never -est.

questions.text: Timur's scarf is long, dark, and woollen. The correct order of adjectives is: "a beautiful ___ dark woollen scarf".
questions.hint: Order: opinion → SIZE → colour → material. beautiful (opinion) → LONG (size) → dark (colour) → woollen (material). "a beautiful LONG dark woollen scarf" ✅

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses a comparative adjective with "much"?
opts: Sunday is much better than Saturday.
Sunday is much more better than Saturday.
Sunday is the much best day.
Sunday is much the better of Saturday.
questions.correct: Sunday is much better than Saturday.
questions.hint: "MUCH + comparative" = намного: "much BETTER than." ✅ "much more better" is double comparative — wrong! "much the better" is not a standard form.

questions.text: What does "mild" mean when describing weather?
opts: Very cold and difficult to bear
Not too cold and not too hot; pleasantly moderate
Wet and rainy with strong winds
questions.correct: Not too cold and not too hot; pleasantly moderate
questions.hint: "When Aizat arrived in September, the weather was MILD and warm." MILD = мягкий, умеренный. The opposite of harsh or extreme.

questions.text: "Relentless" rain means it rains for a short time and then quickly stops.
questions.hint: RELENTLESS = never stopping, continuing without rest or pause. "The wind in Astana is sharp, dry, and RELENTLESS — it never stops." The opposite of brief or light.

questions.text: A jacket that does not allow water to pass through, even in heavy rain, is called ___.
questions.hint: WATERPROOF = водонепроницаемый. "Timur wears a long WATERPROOF jacket with a hood on rainy days." Water cannot get through it — the key feature for wet weather.

questions.text: What does "durable" mean?
opts: Light and thin — easy to carry
Strong and long-lasting; able to survive regular use
Bright and colourful; easy to see in the dark
questions.correct: Strong and long-lasting; able to survive regular use
questions.hint: "These boots are more DURABLE than any others I have tried." DURABLE = прочный, долговечный — built to last a long time without breaking.

questions.text: What is a "lining" in a piece of clothing?
opts: The outer layer that protects from rain
The pattern printed on the fabric
A layer of material on the inside of a coat or hat
The zip or buttons on the front
questions.correct: A layer of material on the inside of a coat or hat
questions.hint: "The hood has a soft fleece LINING on the inside." LINING = подкладка — the inner layer that adds warmth and comfort.

questions.text: "Freezing" weather means it is slightly cool — pleasant for a walk in the park.
questions.hint: FREEZING = extremely cold — much colder than just "cool." "My hands are absolutely FREEZING!" — it means dangerously cold, not slightly cool. Cool is pleasant; freezing is not!

questions.text: The bottom part of a shoe or boot that touches the ground is called the ___.
questions.hint: SOLE = подошва. "The thick rubber SOLE of Timur's boots does not slip on icy pavements." The sole is the very bottom part — in contact with the ground.

questions.text: What does "essential" mean in "The scarf, hat and gloves are absolutely essential"?
opts: Fashionable and stylish in the current season
Cheap and easy to find in any shop
Optional but nice to have in cold weather
questions.hint: "The scarf, hat and gloves are simple but absolutely ESSENTIAL." ESSENTIAL = необходимый, обязательный — you cannot go without it. Without them, even the warmest coat is not enough.
